reference.title: Sword with Scabbard
reference.rights: Public Domain, per Met object page

camera.view_angle: near-orthographic frontal, slight downward tilt; blade and scabbard lie parallel in image plane
camera.uncertainty: low for in-plane proportions; high for depth/thickness and cross-section

observed_landmarks.name: pommel
observed_landmarks.visible_evidence: dark lobed/domed metal cap at grip top

observed_landmarks.name: grip
observed_landmarks.visible_evidence: brown cylindrical grip between pommel and guard, with small circular fitting

observed_landmarks.name: guard
observed_landmarks.visible_evidence: wide dark metal crossguard with openwork/scrolled ends

observed_landmarks.name: blade_shoulder
observed_landmarks.visible_evidence: blade emerges below guard, edges taper from shoulder

observed_landmarks.name: blade_mid
observed_landmarks.visible_evidence: bright steel, straight double-edged profile, faint central ridge line

proposed_parts.how_it_connects: caps grip tang; likely peened or pinned

proposed_parts.visible_region: brown cylinder between pommel and guard
proposed_parts.how_it_connects: encases tang between pommel and guard
slides over tang, seats against blade shoulders

proposed_parts.visible_region: long bright steel from guard to tip
proposed_parts.how_it_connects: integral with tang passing through grip; shoulders abut guard
continuous with blade, threaded/peened at pommel

ambiguous_features: blade cross-section (diamond vs lenticular vs ridged) not determinable from frontal view
tang construction and pommel attachment hidden
surface wear/patina may obscure ridge lines

boundary: Part coordinates are observations/proposals from the image stage, not manually supplied universal sword coordinates. The builder uses the accepted geometry contract separately.
